claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in HEAs is governed by the formation and maintenance of a mechanically robust, self-healing, multi-element passive oxide layer.
The passive layer is enriched in corrosion-resistant species supplied by the HEA constituent elements.
The passive layer reduces surface wear damage.
The passive layer limits corrosive attack.
The proposed baseline HEA has a homogeneous microstructure.
The proposed baseline composition forms moderately protective passive oxides under ambient conditions.
Increasing the proportion of elements that favor robust passivation will enhance formation of a stable, multicomponent passive oxide.
Passive-layer composition, thickness, and mechanical integrity mediate tribocorrosion resistance.
An enhanced passive layer lowers material removal by supplying mechanical protection during sliding wear.
The enhanced passive layer acts as a barrier to corrosive species.
The HEA's multielement composition enables the passive layer to self-heal after wear damage.
Self-healing of the passive layer diminishes the synergistic interaction between wear and corrosion.
The modified HEA will have a lower wear rate than the baseline under matched tribocorrosion conditions.
The modified HEA will have a lower corrosion current density than the baseline under matched tribocorrosion conditions.
The modified HEA will exhibit less overall tribocorrosion degradation than the baseline.
The predicted benefit requires passive-film regeneration to keep pace with mechanically and chemically induced damage.
Excessive abrasion can strip the oxide faster than it reforms and thereby cause the mechanism to fail.
Aggressive chemical environments can destabilize the passive film and thereby cause the mechanism to fail.
